title: Home 2-Week Supply
description: Use this list to grow your 72-hour kit into a supply that lets you stay home safely for two weeks without stores, power, or running water.

sources.title: Survival Basics: Sanitation and Waste Management (EM 9334)
Avoid Foodborne Illness During Temporary Power Outages

items.text: Water: 14 gallons (53 L) per person (1 gallon per person per day), stored in sealed food-grade containers, plus more for pets
A way to treat more water: unscented bleach (check the label for disinfection directions), a filter, or a safe way to boil
2 weeks of shelf-stable food your family eats: canned meat, beans, soup, fruit, vegetables, peanut butter, cereal, rice, pasta
As large a reserve of daily prescriptions as your doctor and insurance allow, rotated so it stays fresh
A safe way to cook without power (camp stove or grill used outdoors only) and extra fuel stored outside the living space
Battery carbon monoxide alarms on every level and near bedrooms
2-week sanitation kit: bag-lined bucket toilet with lid, heavy trash bags, toilet paper, disinfectant, and gloves
Enough flashlights, lanterns, and batteries for 14 nights
Battery or hand-crank radio with spare batteries
Safe heat plan for winter (warm bedding, layers, one heated room) and cooling plan for summer (cooling center location)
Well-stocked home first aid kit with extra gauze, tape, and oral rehydration salts
Appliance thermometers in the fridge and freezer, coolers, and a plan to get ice
Manual can opener and basic cooking pot, utensils, and dish soap
Hygiene supplies for 2 weeks: soap, hand sanitizer, wipes, toothpaste, menstrual supplies, diapers
Ways to charge phones: power banks, a car charger, or a small solar panel or power station
Cash in small bills for several days of food, fuel, and supplies
Food and medicine for pets for 2 weeks
Fire extinguisher and smoke alarms with fresh batteries
Basic tools: wrench for utilities, hammer, pry bar, tarps, duct tape, and work gloves
Extra trash bags and a plan to store garbage sealed and away from the house
Books, games, and offline entertainment
Build it slowly - add a few cans or a case of water each shopping trip instead of panic-buying
Rotate food and water: eat oldest first, check dates once a year, and replace what you use
